BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Several positions would move significant risk to Wattlebridge: a cap shortfall of AUD 1.2m, deductible thresholds, title and tax claims under the general regime, and open conditions on Bluefen and Riverlark. We should not accept any of these as drafted. This is a commercial and legal review for the deal team, not a substitute for sign-off by the responsible NSW solicitor.

## 1. Departures from the Playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Start 25% / AUD 6m. 20% is a fallback usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority naming the draft. None given. | Reject. Counter at 25%. Do not offer 20% without written authority. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Counter at AUD 5,000. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, deductible (only excess recoverable) | AUD 50,000, once exceeded seller liable from first dollar | Reject. Counter at AUD 50,000 tipping basket. |
| General time limit (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval) | Counter at 24 months. |
| Time limits applied to all claims | Apply to all Claims unless expressly stated | Fundamental/Title claims are a separate regime | Reject. |
| Fundamental/Title (capacity, title) | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject outright. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of them, to the maximum enforceable extent, non-waivable | Reject. Add fraud carve-out. |
| Disclosure (Schedule 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public searches | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room, public-register and deemed disclosure | Reject. Delete 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | No claim for any matter the Buyer or advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | Delete 8.3. |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery | Effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Reject. Make a condition precedent. |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Release provided after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval. | Reject. Require payout at Completion from price. |
| Employee bonuses (DL 5; funds flow) | AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller", not in funds flow | Specific line item or seller-funded, including triggered on-costs | Require a specific line item or seller funding, with on-costs quantified. |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure. AUD 180,000 not independently verified. | Reject as drafted. Broaden and retain the cure. |
| Export/privacy incident (4.6; DL 6) | "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand. | Require investigation and updates. Do not characterise it either way. |
| Sandbar renewals (DL 8) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess. No automatic debt classification or price deduction. | Require contracts and assess. No automatic deduction. |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Keep separate. Terms OPEN. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. | Reject. Treat as open, outside the general regime. |
| Title (DL 10) | Share register at DD-012 evidences title | DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. Require independent evidence. | Require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence. |

## 2. Reasoning on the Material Issues

**Cap, thresholds and time limits combined.** These do not operate in isolation. Under the Seller's terms, a AUD 300,000 claim would recover only AUD 50,000 after the basket. Under our playbook it would recover the full AUD 300,000. The AUD 1.2m cap shortfall, the 18-month period and the deductible basket compound each other. The Seller's package is materially weaker on every axis at once.

**Fundamental/Title.** Putting capacity and title under general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity" moves our most important protections into the general regime. Title is the core asset warranty for a 100% share purchase. This is a non-starter.

**Limitations and non-reliance without a fraud carve-out.** The Seller's clauses apply to "all Claims of any nature" and contain no fraud carve-out. Combined with the Seller's data-room disclosure and buyer-knowledge exclusion, the Seller could argue that a Buyer's knowledge of a discoverable matter bars a claim even where the Seller concealed the matter. The fraud carve-out is a hard requirement and cannot be waived.

**Disclosure and buyer knowledge.** Disclosure of the whole data room and public registers, together with clause 8.3, would shift the burden of finding breaches onto the Buyer. The disclosure letter's own paragraphs 2 to 10 identify specific open items, which shows the Seller knows where the issues are. Those specific items should be disclosed specifically, not buried under general disclosure.

**Bluefen (AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue).** The Seller's own disclosure confirms there is no final written consent and no evidence that conditions are satisfied. "Consent treated as satisfied on delivery" would leave us exposed to a material customer relationship with no consent in hand. This should be a CP with evidence of conditions before Completion.

**Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m).** The Seller's disclosure confirms the facility has not been repaid. Under a debt-free, cash-free price, the Seller should discharge it from proceeds at Completion. A post-completion release leaves the security over the business open, and the Buyer carries the risk. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.

**Employee bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs).** The funds flow excludes these, so either the Buyer pays them post-Completion or they are silently dropped. Neither is acceptable. The on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are unquantified and must be added to the line item or seller-funded.

**Ironquay (AUD 180,000).** The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment, and the Seller's disclosure says transfer of project materials depends on cleared payment, with no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified in either direction. We should broaden the indemnity and keep the SOW3 cure so that we can resolve payment and secure the materials.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006).** The disclosure describes a preliminary investigation involving ~1,240 records containing names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps, sent to an unintended external address. We do not know whether anyone accessed it, the scope, or whether notification is required. Our playbook requires us to preserve logs, investigate and receive updates, without characterising the incident as a confirmed breach or assigning a loss. A specific indemnity or covenant is a judgment call for the deal team, since the playbook does not address it directly. I would flag it for decision rather than assume it.

**Sandbar (AUD 330,000).** The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs, but the disclosure states it is unknown whether each is unavoidable, terminable or accrued, and the renewals appear in two data-room items (DD-008 and DD-011). We should review the contracts and their timing before deciding whether any adjustment is needed. No automatic price deduction or debt classification.

**Tax/IP and title.** The Seller's claim that tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime" is not accurate under our playbook, which treats them as open. The DD-012 register is a Seller-supplied source. It is not independent proof of title, so we need an independent search and confirmation of authority.

**Other items not covered by the playbook.** The office lease (DL 7) and Mossvale assignment restriction (DL 9) are flagged as notification and consent questions, not confirmed consent requirements. We should confirm with the Seller whether any consent is needed for the share sale and treat any consent as a condition if required.

## 3. Summary of Recommendations

1. **Reject the Seller draft as a basis for negotiation.** Mark up from our playbook baseline.
2. **Cap:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not offer 20% without Amelia Frost's prior written authority naming this draft.
3. **Thresholds:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket.
4. **Time:** 24 months general. Fundamental/Title at least 6 years.
5. **Fundamental/Title:** Separate regime, 100% cap, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
6. **Fraud carve-out:** Add to all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clauses, non-waivable.
7. **Disclosure:** Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
8. **Clause 8.3:** Delete. Any knowledge qualifier needs named persons and reasonable enquiry, and never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
9. **Bluefen:** CP requiring effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion.
10. **Riverlark:** Repay at Completion from proceeds. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
11. **Bonuses:** Specific line item in funds flow, including quantified on-costs, or seller-funded.
12. **Ironquay:** Broaden the indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure.
13. **Export incident:** Require log preservation, investigation and updates. Flag any specific indemnity for deal-team decision.
14. **Sandbar:** Review contracts. No automatic deduction or debt classification.
15. **Tax/IP:** Keep open and outside the general regime. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
16. **Title:** Require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is not sufficient.
17. **Confirm** whether the office lease or Mossvale arrangements require consent for the share sale.
